newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies end mixed, marks, yen finish lower.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies end mixed, marks, yen finish lower.

text.p: IMM currency futures finished mixed, as marks and yen deepened losses due to anticipation about the European Union's summit in Amsterdam on Monday, traders and currency analysts said.

"There are indications that they must come out with some euro agreement going forward, but there is no way they can go in with the conditions they previously established," Pat Donahue, head of the forex desk at Nationsbank, said.
At Monday's meeting, EU leaders are scheduled to finalize the budget discipline pact that was informally reached in Dublin last year.
However, France and Germany failed to reach agreement at their one-day meeting on Friday, with France saying that Europe needed time for discussions on the budget accord.

While French president Jacques Chirac said negotiations were going in the right direction, one government source said a EU jobs and growth pact proposed by France must have the same weight as the stability pact limiting budget deficits.
"The social aspect cannot be an annex, it has to have the same weight as the stability pact," the source told reporters after the Franco-German summit.
The key IMM currencies, yen, marks and Swiss francs, succumbed to selling pressure after attempting to rally on the U.S. May Producer Price Index (PPI).
Overall and core PPI fell 0.3 percent, compared to average trade estimates for declines of 0.1 percent in both rates.
The data suggested the U.S. Federal Reserve would not tighten rates at their July 1-2 meeting, and immediately pressured the dollar, traders said.
September marks rose to $0.5829, but failed to touch resistance at $0.5833 which then corresponded to the key support level of 1.7260 spot marks.
However, the data sparked a strong rally in both U.S. bonds and U.S. stocks, which fueled further demand for dollars and erased the light bid in key currencies, traders said.
"The dollar is simply bid because you have conditions in the U.S. that are just terrific," Donahue said.
September marks slid through the contract low settlement of $0.5819 and through the one-week low that was set overnight on GLOBEX at $0.5811.
Later in the day, the contract eased below support at $0.5786, which corresponded to dollar/mark resistance at 1.74 spot.
Meanwhile September yen continued to grind below support at $0.008820 or 114.90 spot.
September Canadian dollars remained higher, but failed to re-test resistance at $0.7310 or about 1.3766 spot.

At the end of pit trade, September yen was off $0.000055 at $0.008820, marks were off $0.0032 at $0.5790, Swiss francs were $0.0002 lower at $0.7005, sterling was $0.0048 higher at $1.6328, Canadian dollars were up $0.0015 at $0.7291, Australian dollars were $0.0007 lower at $0.7514 and Mexican pesos were $0.000100 higher at $0.120800.
